iconicAnchor.label: Finished botanical watercolor plates balancing structural accuracy and painterly color
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: Kew describes botanical art as an art-and-science practice in which accurate structure, scale, color, and selective detail make a plant legible beyond what a photograph alone can show.

sources.title: What is botanical art?
supports: Botanical artists study anatomy, scale, attachment, and hidden structures to produce truthful plant representations.
Watercolor, pencil, and pen can be selected and combined to describe the specimen's important features.

sources.title: Artists in the Florilegium
supports: Botanical watercolor can build depth and fine detail through layered washes while preserving close observation and scale.
Professional botanical painters balance clarity, truth to the plant, character, and an economy of brushwork.
